sections.label: CPF transfers to spouses
sections.summary: The CPF Act is amended so members aged 55 and above can transfer CPF savings, including Retirement Account savings, to spouses if they set aside the Basic Retirement Sum.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: We are now amending the CPF Act to enable CPF Board to implement these changes more directly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: We are amending the CPF Act to make it directly explicit that CPF members aged 55 and above can transfer savings from their CPF accounts, including their Retirement Account (RA), to their spouses if they have set aside the Basic Retirement Sum (BRS).

sections.label: Expanding incapacity definition
sections.summary: The CPF Act is amended to expand incapacity to include members with terminal illness or total permanent disability who still work in diminished capacity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Currently, members with terminal illnesses or total permanent disability but can still do some form of work, do not fall within this definition of incapacity and, hence, do not qualify to make claims under HPS and DPS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: We are amending the CPF Act to expand the definition of incapacity to include members with terminal illness and total permanent disability who may still be working or able to do some form of work, but in a diminished capacity.

sections.label: MediSave claim penalties
sections.summary: The amendment lets CPF Board impose administrative penalties on medical institutions and approved insurers making wrong or unauthorised MediSave claims or failing audits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: To strengthen the safeguards over MediSave claims, this amendment will allow CPF Board to impose administrative penalties on medical institutions and approved insurers that make wrong or unauthorised claims on members' MediSave monies or do not comply with audits ordered by CPF Board or other administrative requirements.

sections.label: Withdrawing government scheme payouts
sections.summary: The amendment allows CPF members to withdraw cash payouts credited under Government schemes, such as GST Voucher, without existing CPF withdrawal rules.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: The second example is to allow CPF members to apply to withdraw cash payouts that were credited to their accounts under various Government schemes, such as the GST Voucher.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: As these payouts are meant to support members' daily needs, this amendment will allow members to withdraw these credited monies without being subject to existing CPF withdrawal rules.

sections.label: HPS coverage and claims
sections.summary: As of 2013 about 70% of HDB flat owners were covered by HPS, and in 2012 there were 1,074 claims totalling $89.8 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to CPF, as of 2013, about 70% of all HDB flat owners were covered by HPS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2012, a total of 1,074 claims amounting to $89.8 million were made to HPS policyholders.

sections.label: HPS rebates in 2015
sections.summary: In August 2015 CPF paid at least $400 in HPS rebates to each of 470,000 Singaporeans and Permanent Residents on HPS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In August 2015, CPF paid out more than at least $400 in HPS rebates to each of the 470,000 Singaporeans and Permanent Residents (PRs) on HPS.

sections.label: Informing homeowners about HPS benefits
sections.summary: The Ministry should regularly inform homeowners of the scheme's benefits and consider including Singaporeans with pre-existing illnesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With a rising senior citizen population and constant reminders in the press about how Singaporeans do not plan well for retirement, the Ministry should step up its efforts to constantly inform homeowners of the benefits of the scheme every few years through brochures and pamphlets as they service their mortgages and seriously look at including Singaporeans with pre-existing illnesses to improve the scheme further.

sections.label: Claims for terminal illness and disability
sections.summary: Insured CPF members may claim for terminal illness and total permanent disability even if not incapacitated from employment, in specified situations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under the proposed amendments, a CPF member who is insured under the scheme will now be allowed to make a claim under the scheme for terminal illness and total permanent disability, even though the member is not incapacitated from ever continuing in any employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I note that the same change is also effected in the same Bill for DPS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, it seems to me, from a plain reading of the amendment Bill, that the only situations where a member can make a claim under the scheme for terminal illness and total permanent disability, even though the member is not incapacitated from ever continuing in any employment, are if (a) the member is suffering from terminal illness and is said by a registered medical practitioner to be expected to result in death within 12 months or (b) the member has suffered total or permanent disability of less than two eyes, two limbs or one eye and one limb.

sections.label: Non-spouse co-owner paying HPS premium
sections.summary: The Bill allows a non-spouse co-owner of a property to pay the HPS premium of the other co-owner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Bill also seeks to allow a non-spouse member who is a co-owner of a property to pay the premium for the HPS scheme of the other co-owner.

sections.label: Choosing CPF LIFE plan later
sections.summary: Members will only need to choose their CPF LIFE plan closer to the start of payouts, between their PEA and up to age 70.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With the amendments, members will now only need to choose their CPF LIFE plan closer to the start of their CPF LIFE payouts, which can be anytime between their PEA or, if they choose, up to age 70.

sections.label: Median CPF savings by gender
sections.summary: In 2013, median CPF savings for women aged 51 to 54 were about $90,000, compared to about $130,000 for males.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In 2013, the median CPF savings for women aged 51 to 54 were about $90,000, compared to males in that age group which is about $130,000.

sections.label: Co-owners' OA paying HPS premiums
sections.summary: The amendment allows OA savings of other co-owners, such as children, parents or siblings, to pay HPS premiums of insured members who have run out of OA savings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Similarly, this amendment also allows the OA savings of other co-owners, whether it is their children, parents or siblings, to help pay for the HPS premiums of insured members who have run out of OA savings.

sections.label: MediSave recovery and CPF amendments
sections.summary: The change mandates recovery of mistakenly deducted MediSave monies from medical institutions and approved insurers, and refunds for uncompleted treatments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: While the Minister shared that there are not many cases, every case, to any person whose MediSave funds are important, is one case too many, as we all know.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: So, I am glad that this change is being done because what it does is that it not only sets aside the penalty framework, it also mandates the recovery of MediSave monies from the medical institutions as well as the approved insurers for those that have been mistakenly deducted as well as refunds for monies from the institutions due to uncompleted medical treatments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments to the CPF Act are welcomed as they will benefit members with greater flexibility and enhance support and protection in the use of their CPF funds to build their retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It does not, however, address the frustration that members have expressed with regard to the complexity and changes in the CPF schemes when they do happen.

sections.label: CPF members paying home premium
sections.summary: The amendment is expected to help about 1,000 to 2,000 CPF members overcome a home owner's inability to pay the premium.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The amendment today, we believe, will help maybe 1,000 to 2,000 CPF members to overcome the inability of the home owner to pay the premium.

sections.label: PEA revision in 2007
sections.summary: The last revision to PEA was in 2007, when it was raised from age 62 to 65.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The last time we made a revision to PEA was in 2007, when we raised PEA from the age of 62 to 65.

sections.label: Deferment increases monthly pay-out
sections.summary: For every year of deferment, a member is expected to receive about 6% more every month permanently from the pay-out date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: For every year of deferment, he is expected to receive about 6% more every month permanently from the date of the pay-out.

sections.label: Penalties for MediSave deduction errors
sections.summary: The amendment sends a clear message to medical institutions and approved insurers, mandating recovery and giving CPF Board the right to impose administrative penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In fact, we are stepping up our efforts and one of our objectives for this amendment is to send a very clear message to medical institutions and approved insurers that we take this seriously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Whenever we discover any case of error, first, we mandate the recovery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: And second, Page: 97 with this amendment, CPF Board will have the right to impose administrative penalties as well.

sections.label: HPS and pre-existing conditions
sections.summary: Only those with fairly severe pre-existing conditions such as cancer, kidney and heart diseases will have their HPS applications rejected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: After all, surely the original intention of the scheme is to provide peace of mind to all members who have taken loans to pay for their HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: So, only those who suffer from fairly severe pre-existing conditions, such as cancer, kidney and heart diseases, will have their applications rejected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In fact, I would like to clarify that HPS is not mandatory for members with severe pre-existing conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We do whatever we can, including this amendment, to help them stay with HPS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: So, for those who due to their medical conditions and had their applications rejected, are excluded from HPS.
